summary: Redwood AE+SE demo of logging and retention controls in the Console and API, focusing on request storage toggles, PII redaction, audit logs, and keys integration. Customer concerned about retention for marketing PII, compliance (PCI/HIPAA questions surfaced), and wanting a non-logging mode for sensitive endpoints. Agreed next steps: send security artifacts, run a benchmark/pilot with request_storage=false, and follow up with compliance examples.
topics: Demo: Console toggles - request storage, redaction rules
API flags and SDK behavior (request_storage, redact_fields)
transcript:
[00:00] Maya Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. I'm Maya from Redwood, I'm the AE on the account. With me is Arjun, our SE who will lead the demo. Quick intros?
[00:12] Lena Ortiz: Hi I'm Lena, head of data science at Horizon Retail. We're mainly here to make sure we can comply with retention norms for customer PII in chatbots and the marketing touchpoints.
[00:22] Mark Hollis: Mark here, CTO. Interested in risk and cost tradeoffs.
[00:26] Priya Menon: Priya, compliance. We'll want to confirm what stays, what gets redacted, and how auditable the controls are.
[00:33] Arjun Patel: Great — thanks all. Agenda: show Console toggles for request storage, a quick look at redaction rules in Redwood Optimize/Console, how the API flag behaves, then Q&A.
[01:05] Maya Chen: Quick note — if you want to keep things high-level we'll stay light, Arjun will deep-dive if needed.
[01:24] Arjun Patel: Alright screen-share — pulling up the Horizon demo tenant. First thing, top-level setting: "Request storage" which is a boolean toggle. When off, we don't persist raw request payloads in long-term storage; metadata/audit events still flow to the control plane (and can be backed to customer S3 if you choose).
[01:48] Priya Menon: Wait — metadata still stored? What is "metadata" here?
[01:55] Arjun Patel: Good q. Metadata includes request id, timestamp, model used, token counts, success/failure, and routing info, but not the raw user prompt if request_storage=false. We can also scrub PII from request payloads before any transient storage using redaction rules.
[02:18] Mark Hollis: So with request_storage=false, is anything written to disk on the inference node? We have auditors worried about ephemeral logs.
[02:28] Arjun Patel: At runtime we do transient in-memory processing for inference; logs for debugging might be ephemeral in the worker process but they're not written to durable object storage. We can enable ephemeral-only logging for infra teams and prevent collection. For Dedicated/Private, you can route logs to your VPC logging endpoint — we support S3, GCP buckets, and SIEM integrations.
[02:58] Lena Ortiz: How does the redaction work — do we provide regex rules? Are there prebuilt PII detectors?
[03:06] Arjun Patel: Two approaches: (1) serverside redaction rules you configure in the Console — field-level patterns, regex, and named entity rules, and (2) client-side SDK helpers we provide to pre-scrub before sending. We also have an ML-based PII detector for emails, SSNs, phone numbers that you can apply as a preprocessor. Note: ML detectors have a small false positive/negative rate, so we recommend deterministic rules for critical fields.
[03:35] Priya Menon: Can we get a demo of adding a redaction rule for card numbers and email?
[03:41] Arjun Patel: Sure — switching to the Redaction tab. Creating a rule: name = "card_4_digit_pattern", scope = "requests.chat.message", pattern = "\b(?:\d[ -]*?){13,16}\b" — and choose action = mask with token. Apply immediately or stage to canary.
[04:10] Evan Zhao: Is that enforcement synchronous before the request hits the model or is it async post-process?
[04:16] Arjun Patel: It's synchronous pre-inference. So if a request contains a match it will be masked before hitting the model and the masked copy is what's considered for downstream storage.
[04:30] Maya Chen: Note that masking happens per request; however, metadata like token counts still reflect the masked content — we can show how counts change in the test harness.
[04:40] Lena Ortiz: If we mask in the Console, do we have to change our prompts? We don't want to degrade prompt quality for personalization.
[04:47] Arjun Patel: Two options: mask only storage (so model still receives original content, but storage is masked) — that's request_storage versus storage-only masking; or mask before both storage and model input. The Console makes these explicit: "Mask for storage only" vs "Mask before inference". Many customers choose storage-only for personalization but masked storage for compliance.
[05:10] Mark Hollis: That seems risky — can we keep redaction client-side to avoid sending PII at all?
[05:16] Priya Menon: That's what our legal team prefers, ideally.
[05:19] Arjun Patel: Yes — client-side redaction is supported. We have SDK helpers (JS/Go/Python) with a redactFields helper where you can annotate sensitive keys and the SDK will strip them locally. That option is what we recommend for PCI/PHI-sensitive workloads.
[05:37] [06:00] Maya Chen: Quick poll — what is Horizon's tolerance for sending raw PII to the hosted environment?
[06:07] Priya Menon: Low. We want zero retention for PII, prefer not to send bank or card numbers at all.
[06:13] Lena Ortiz: For marketing, emails are okay transiently but need to be purged T+7 days.
[06:20] Mark Hollis: We also have a regulatory requirement to keep request audit trail for 90 days for certain debug logs — but those must not include PII.
[06:30] Arjun Patel: Perfect — sounds like a mixed policy: client-side redaction for card/bank data, storage-only masking for emails with TTL 7d, audit logs without PII kept for 90d. We can implement that via policies and a routing rule.
[06:50] Arjun Patel: Now API flags — in the REST/SDK you can set request_storage=false, redact_fields=["user_email","payment.card_number"], and sampling=false (sampling affects how much of the logs we keep for model telemetry). I'll show a sample cURL and node snippet.
[07:20] Arjun Patel: (shares code) Example: POST /v1/generate with header X-Redwood-Request-Storage: false and body {"prompt":"...","redact_fields":["user.email"]} — Redwood will honor those at the per-request level; account-level policies can override to be stricter.
[07:48] Lena Ortiz: If we set request_storage=false per request, do we still get usage billing and token counts?
[07:54] Arjun Patel: Yes. Billing is usage-based and token measurement still occurs for invoicing. We can send aggregated token metrics to your billing export without the raw payloads.
[08:10] Evan Zhao: Does the sampling flag affect optimization models? Does it change what data gets used for future model benchmarking?
[08:19] Arjun Patel: Sampling=false means we don't sample that request for telemetry. We won't use it in model quality metrics or in training telemetry. If you want absolutely no telemetry, combine that with request_storage=false and redact_fields. For enterprise/private, telemetry can also be disabled globally.
[08:42] [09:00] Priya Menon: Auditing — how do we prove a redaction happened? We need an immutable audit trail showing original hash and who applied the rule.
[09:09] Arjun Patel: We maintain an audit record for policy actions: rule id, who applied, timestamp, and a redaction-proof hash (HMAC) of the original content that is not reversible. We can also push those audit events to your SIEM or KMS-backed log store. Importantly, the hash lets you verify content existed without revealing it.
[09:40] Mark Hollis: KMS — do you let us use our key?
[09:44] Arjun Patel: Yes. For Private and Dedicated we support customer-managed keys (CMK) via AWS KMS, GCP KMS, or HSM. The control plane metadata is encrypted and you can manage rotation/POKs.
[09:58] Lena Ortiz: Performance — does masking or pre/post-redaction add latency?
[10:05] Arjun Patel: Minimal for regex rules — we benchmarked sub-5ms overhead at 99th percentile for typical patterns. ML-based PII detection is a bit heavier but still in the low tens of ms depending on sequence length. We show in the Console expected latency impact per ruleset.
[10:30] Evan Zhao: Show us a quick benchmark with and without masking on a 3k token prompt.
[10:36] Arjun Patel: Running the built-in test harness — baseline avg latency 320ms; with regex masking applied pre-inference 330ms; with ML detector pre-inference 360ms. These are approximations — actual numbers vary by model and infra.
[11:05] Maya Chen: Re SOC2/Compliance — Priya, you asked for manifest of controls — we have SOC2 Type II and ISO docs, and a compliance mapping sheet that covers redaction and retention controls. We'll attach those.
[11:20] Priya Menon: Do you handle e-discovery or support legal hold?
[11:25] Arjun Patel: We support legal hold flags — if set, retention TTL is extended and the request is kept in a locked bucket. Legal hold is auditable and requires admin approval; we can show RBAC controls in the Console.
[11:40] Mark Hollis: On RBAC — can we restrict who can flip request_storage at the account level vs project level?
[11:46] Arjun Patel: Yes. RBAC supports roles: Admin, Compliance, Dev, Read-only. Only Admins or designated Compliance roles can change account-level retention. Project-level overrides are allowed if policy permits.
[12:02] Lena Ortiz: Any gotchas with function calling and tool outputs? We occasionally store tool responses that include PII.
[12:10] Arjun Patel: Function/tool outputs are treated like request responses; redaction rules apply to response channels too. For function calls, we recommend marking the call as sensitive in the SDK so the platform applies end-to-end masking.
[12:26] [12:50] Maya Chen: Ok let's open the Console activity log to show an example redaction event.
[12:57] Arjun Patel: Here you see an event: request id, rule applied, masked fields, HMAC of original content, and link to audit export. The UI shows a timeline and you can download CSV for compliance review.
[13:20] Priya Menon: Is the HMAC computed with our KMS key?
[13:24] Arjun Patel: We can compute HMAC with a customer key in Dedicated/Private; for hosted customers we compute using a platform key but we can support customer key exchange if needed.
[13:36] [14:00] Lena Ortiz: For our pilot we want two flows: (A) marketing emails — mask in storage, keep model input as-is, TTL 7d; (B) payments — client-side redaction, never stored, no telemetry. How quick to set up?
[14:14] Maya Chen: We'll put together a pilot plan. Typical pilot timeline is 2–4 weeks to configure policies and run sample traffic. Arjun, do you agree?
[14:21] Arjun Patel: Yep. For flow A we can configure Console policies and show sample reporting within 2–3 days. For flow B we'll provide SDK snippets and a secure checklist; integration could be as fast as a week depending on your engineering bandwidth.
[14:36] Mark Hollis: Any cost delta for the masking/detection?
[14:40] Arjun Patel: Regex masking has no extra cost. ML-based PII detection is billed as a light preprocessor cost (fraction of a token-based unit). We'll provide a cost estimate for expected throughput — that's part of the follow up materials.
[14:58] [15:20] Priya Menon: For legal and procurement: do you offer contractual clauses for data handling and deletion? We need them for our procurement team.
[15:28] Maya Chen: Yes — enterprise contracts include bespoke data handling addendums: deletion SLAs, audit rights, and data residency clauses. We'll share a template.
[15:40] Evan Zhao: About logs exported to our S3 — can we get them delivered encrypted with our KMS key and put in a locked bucket?
[15:47] Arjun Patel: Yes for Dedicated/Private we support direct S3 delivery encrypted with your CMK and we can configure lifecycle rules. For hosted we can push to an S3 export; encryption depends on the integration mode but we support server-side encryption and external key wrapping.
[16:05] Maya Chen: Quick demo of the Optimize tab — this is where we recommend batching/quantization and show cost vs quality. Not directly retention but it ties to unit economics.
[16:18] Arjun Patel: In Optimize you can create profiles per workload: masked-storage-enabled, low-latency, or cost-optimized. Profiles include default redaction rules and TTL settings so you can apply them consistently.
[16:40] Lena Ortiz: Can the policy be applied via API so our deployment automation can turn on a profile for a given route?
[16:46] Arjun Patel: Yes — everything in Console can be managed via the config API for automation. We'll share the API spec in the follow up.
[17:05] Mark Hollis: One more technical: does masking change the model output deterministically? If we mask names, will personalization break?
[17:12] Arjun Patel: If you apply storage-only masking, model input stays same, so no change. If you mask pre-inference, output may differ; to balance personalization we often do a tokenization-aware image and replace PII tokens with placeholders the model understands, e.g., "[REDACTED_EMAIL]", and then post-process mapping for the UX.
[17:38] [18:00] Priya Menon: Will you share examples we can run through legal?
[18:04] Maya Chen: Yes — we'll send a short repo with examples: SDK usage, server-side rule samples, and an end-to-end pilot guide.
[18:15] Arjun Patel: Technical note: for private deployments (VPC/on-prem) we support an air-gapped deployment where no data leaves customer network; redaction is performed locally and audit logs can be pushed to your SIEM.
[18:30] Lena Ortiz: That could be important for certain regions.
[18:33] Mark Hollis: About rollout: if we start with marketing first and then expand to payments, do you support gradual rollouts/canary?
[18:39] Arjun Patel: Absolutely. Console supports canary policies and route-based rollouts with traffic percentage. You can also set auto-fallback to a non-masked variant if latency spikes.
[19:00] Evan Zhao: One clarification: sampling=false + request_storage=false — does that remove all model telemetry?
[19:07] Arjun Patel: It removes request-level telemetry and prevents the request from being included in quality metrics. Platform-level telemetry like node health is still collected for reliability. For Private you can turn that off too.
[19:28] [19:45] Maya Chen: Wrapping up, quick recap and owners?
[19:50] Priya Menon: We'll write up compliance requirements and list exact PII fields to redact.
[19:55] Lena Ortiz: We'll send sample traffic and a list of example prompts.
[20:00] Mark Hollis: Engineering will evaluate the SDK integration path.
[20:05] Maya Chen: Great — we'll send SOC2, env diagram, sample code, and a recorded demo clip. Arjun will run a small benchmark and set up a pilot tenant.
[20:20] Arjun Patel: I'll also include a sample policy JSON and an API snippet that toggles request_storage.
[20:30] [20:45] Priya Menon: Timelines: we'll aim to have initial decisions by end of next week.
[20:52] Maya Chen: Perfect. Thanks everyone, we'll follow up over email.
[21:00] [END]
